q: Biology， as most people understand it， is the Science of ____.
e: Biology, as most people understand it, is the Science of Life. Biology is the science of life: plants, animals, and microorganisms. Biology systematically studies plants, animals, and microorganisms.

q: They regard it as the study of living things， such as plants， animals and ____.
e: They regard it as the study of living things, such as plants, animals and microorganisms. Microorganisms are microscopic living things such as bacteria, protozoa, and many fungi.

q: The whole world is now suffering under the impact of infectious disease outbreak and weather changes cause by the effect of ____.
e: The whole world is now suffering under the impact of infectious disease outbreak and weather changes cause by the effect of global warming. Global warming is the rise in earth's temperature from extra greenhouse gases.

q: Over fishing， over hunting and deforestation may lead to problems in feeding the world ____ population.
e: Over fishing, over hunting and deforestation may lead to problems in feeding the world exploding population. Overfishing, overhunting, and deforestation make it harder to feed an exploding human population. Deforestation removes forest and can wreck habitat and climate regulation.

q: Many species of plants and animals have disappeared ____.
e: Many species of plants and animals have disappeared forever. When a species is extinct it has disappeared forever. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring.

q: Biology is concerned with animal breeding， agriculture and also in the field of ____ just to mention a few.
e: Biology is concerned with animal breeding, agriculture and also in the field of medicine just to mention a few. Applied biology includes medicine, which restores and maintains human health. Agriculture is crop farming; it is not the same as animal husbandry.

q: Examples include morphology， the study of structure and form of organisms and ____， the study of cell structure and function.
e: Examples include morphology, the study of structure and form of organisms and cytology, the study of cell structure and function. Cytology is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The applied biology includes ____ which is application of biology in productive industry， the medicine and veterinary science.
e: The applied biology includes biotechnology which is application of biology in productive industry, the medicine and veterinary science. Biotechnology uses living systems in industry, medicine, and agriculture. Veterinary science restores and maintains animal health.

q: Biology has strong links with physics， chemistry， geology， geography， mathematics and ____， etc.
e: Biology has strong links with physics, chemistry, geology, geography, mathematics and computer science, etc. Biology also links to computer science, as well as physics and chemistry. Biology is the science of life, not art or history.

q: ____， for example， applies the laws of physics to study the biological processes， like flight of the bird or echolocation in bats.
e: Biophysics, for example, applies the laws of physics to study the biological processes, like flight of the bird or echolocation in bats. Biophysics applies physics to living processes, such as bird flight or bat echolocation. Bats use echolocation; biophysics studies that with the laws of physics.

q: ____ is the study of chemical substances and the chemical processes which occur in the cells and organisms.
e: Biochemistry is the study of chemical substances and the chemical processes which occur in the cells and organisms. Biochemistry studies chemical substances and reactions inside cells.

q: ____ explains how plants and animals are distributed on earth through space and time.
e: Biogeography explains how plants and animals are distributed on earth through space and time. Biogeography tracks distribution of species through space and time.

q: Dichotomous keys provide a simple way to put unknown organisms in their proper ____.
e: Dichotomous keys provide a simple way to put unknown organisms in their proper taxa. Taxa are the ranked groups used in hierarchical classification. A dichotomous key splits identification into two contrasting choices at each step, from general to specific.

q: The word dichotomous is derived from Greek words meaning "divided into two ____".
e: The word dichotomous is derived from Greek words meaning "divided into two parts ". A dichotomous key splits identification into two contrasting choices at each step, from general to specific. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: The method of dichotomous keys is to divide the groups of organisms into two ____ repeatedly.
e: The method of dichotomous keys is to divide the groups of organisms into two categories repeatedly. A dichotomous key splits identification into two contrasting choices at each step, from general to specific. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: They often begin with general characteristics and then progress to more ____ ones step by step.
e: They often begin with general characteristics and then progress to more specific ones step by step. Enzymes are specific: each active site fits a limited set of substrates.

q: By following the sequence of the given dichotomous keys and making the correct choices the unknown organisms can be identified and placed in their proper ____ level.
e: By following the sequence of the given dichotomous keys and making the correct choices the unknown organisms can be identified and placed in their proper taxonomic level. A dichotomous key splits identification into two contrasting choices at each step, from general to specific.

q: Vascular system absent ____
e: Vascular system absent 2. A vascular system of xylem and phloem is missing in bryophytes.

q: Vascular system present ____
e: Vascular system present 3. A vascular system of xylem and phloem is missing in bryophytes.

q: No embryo formation ..... ____
e: No embryo formation Thallophyta. Thallophytes have a simple body with no true embryo in the classical scheme. A true embryo is part of the higher-plant life cycle; thallophytes were defined without that.

q: Has spores and gametes formation ____
e: Has spores and gametes formation Bryophyta. Bryophytes are non-vascular plants such as mosses. Gametes are sex cells: sperm and eggs, produced by meiosis.

q: Spore-bearing... ____
e: Spore-bearing Pteridophyta. Pteridophytes are vascular, seedless plants such as ferns. Ferns and mosses spread by spores, not by flowers.

q: Seed-bearing........ ____
e: Seed-bearing 4. Seed plants are gymnosperms and angiosperms.

q: Non-flowering plants........ ____
e: Non-flowering plants Gymnospermae. Gymnosperms have vascular tissue and seeds but do not make flowers. Flowering is the mark of angiosperms.

q: Flowering plants .. ____
e: Flowering plants. Angiospermae. Flowering is the mark of angiosperms.

q: Cold-blooded animals Warm-blooded animals ____
e: Cold-blooded animals Warm-blooded animals 2. 2 is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Body covered with scales. ____
e: Body covered with scales. 4. Scales without feathers point toward reptiles in simple keys.

q: Body not covered with scales. ____
e: Body not covered with scales. Amphibian. Amphibians can use skin, mouth lining, and lungs for gas exchange. Scales without feathers point toward reptiles in simple keys.

q: Feathers present on body ..............____
e: Feathers present on body Bird. Birds are warm-blooded vertebrates with feathers, not fur. Feathers mark birds in a vertebrate key, not mammals.

q: Hair present on body ____
e: Hair present on body Mammal. Mammals are warm-blooded vertebrates with hair and milk. Hair or fur is a mammal feature in simple vertebrate keys.

q: Has fins ____
e: Has fins Fish. Fish typically use gills; aquatic turtles more often use lungs and accessory surfaces.

q: Has four limbs or without limbs.. ____
e: Has four limbs or without limbs. Reptile. Reptiles are scaly, air-breathing vertebrates that usually use lungs. Four major environment components together are called the ecosphere.
